before: Inferring gear microgeometry from transmission error requires distinguishing contact sensitivity from geometrical recovery. For a quasistatic operator with fixed geometry and compliance, we prove that nonnegative dedendum relief outside loaded support is exactly invisible, and extend the result to coupled linear elastic contact. An implicit contact tangent connects invariance with local sensitivities and the resolution of a discretized relief field. Profile likelihood and Monte Carlo experiments separate exact invariance from weak practical identifiability: for the nominal pair, median scaled dedendum error falls from 0.394 to 0.106 when the relief start moves deeper into contact, using 100 realizations, 120 observations, 300 Nm and 0.1 µm Gaussian noise. Equal-budget controls reveal angular-sampling effects and no statistically resolved benefit of the tested two-load allocation. Same-operator restricted fits across four compliance formulations preserve the distinction between marginal and deeper support. A finite-element contact comparison isolates a dedendum response of 0.179 µm RMS, close to the analytical 0.197 µm, yet an addendum-only inverse attains the same residual and dedendum profiles remain flat. An eight-phase material-removal control gives 0.4–2.1 nm centred changes outside contact, delimiting exact invariance to fixed compliance. None of four formulations meets the adopted 5% research target on twelve external amplitude references. With 200 paired realizations, a 5% gain raises deeper-case median scaled error from 0.0916 to 1.86; the 95% paired-bootstrap median-difference interval is 1.44–3.32. The results delimit operator-conditioned observability without establishing physical profile recovery.
after: Inferring gear microgeometry from transmission error requires distinguishing exact invisibility from weak sensitivity and operator discrepancy. We prove that nonnegative relief outside loaded support is exactly invisible under fixed geometry and compliance, including coupled tooth pairs. Synthetic likelihood and Monte Carlo studies show that nonzero local sensitivity does not guarantee reliable depth and start recovery. A 5% gain perturbation raises deeper-case median scaled error from 0.0916 to 1.86 across 200 paired realizations. Fixed-normal finite-element controls detect a dedendum signal while allowing compensating inverse profiles. A separate bilateral moving-contact model resolves 120 stations for three profiles at two resolutions, including 18 stations omitted by the earlier generator. Its fine-grid isolated, mean-removed dedendum signal is 0.243 µm RMS; the corresponding refinement difference is 0.015 µm. Equal-count inverse designs assess the added stations under nominal-elasticity approximation. Inverse estimates shift with reference resolution despite small transmission residuals. Discrete contact verification and selected independent-solver checks support operator-conditioned conclusions, without establishing continuum-converged reconstruction or physical profile recovery. The resulting protocol checks loaded support, numerical discrepancy and restricted alternatives before inversion.

before: Research question and contributions. We ask which coordinates of a pinion profile modification can be inferred from mean-removed quasistatic transmission error, and when. The paper makes four contributions. (i) A sufficient condition, with proof, under which nonnegative dedendum relief is exactly invisible to transmission error, for independent pair compliance and for symmetric positive-definite coupled compliance. (ii) An implicit contact tangent that connects this invariance with local rank, with sensitivity near the support boundary and with the null space of a discretized relief field. (iii) A comparison, through profile likelihood, Monte Carlo inversion, fixed-budget sampling controls and restricted addendum-only fits, of exact invariance and practical non-identifiability. (iv) A cross-operator assessment, with finite-element contact data, mesh, interface and material-removal controls and an external amplitude benchmark, of what these results imply for physical profile recovery. From them we derive a pre-inversion support check (Section 3.3) for the declared contact model and intended observations.

before: The cross-operator experiments distinguish detecting a relief effect from reconstructing its geometry. Their isolated 24/24 dedendum signal is close to the analytical prediction. That agreement concerns an RMS response difference, not agreement of complete waveforms, stiffness fields or inverse parameters. Restricted fits and profile objectives test whether an addendum-only model explains the data and whether depth and start can compensate for each other. Bulk refinement stabilizes the isolated signal but leaves substantial changes in the inverse residual, so mesh-independent inverse recovery is not established. The inability to identify dedendum in the retained FE observations does not establish insufficiency of all possible observations. Transition phases omitted by this generator may contain additional information; their value cannot be quantified as FE evidence until their contact is resolved. Interpretation remains conditional on the phase mask, parameter bounds, numerical mesh and assumed 0.1 µm objective scale. In particular, deterministic discrepancy prevents a nominal likelihood threshold from certifying physical confidence intervals.
after: The cross-operator experiments distinguish detecting a relief effect from reconstructing its geometry. The isolated 24/24 fixed-normal dedendum signal is close to the analytical prediction, but this agreement concerns an RMS response difference, not complete waveforms or inverse parameters. Restricted fits and profile objectives test compensating alternatives. In that historical study, bulk refinement stabilizes the isolated signal while substantial inverse-residual changes remain. Its 102 retained observations cannot establish insufficiency of all possible observations. Section 4.9 supplies a separate bilateral moving-contact generator at all 120 stations and tests equal-count designs including the former omissions. It retains closure and refinement discrepancies and explicitly measures the nominal-elasticity inverse approximation at the truth. These calculations do not retroactively change the historical fixed-normal data or certify continuum-converged inversion. Interpretation remains conditional on phase design, bounds, mesh, operator and objective scale; deterministic discrepancy prevents a nominal likelihood threshold from certifying physical confidence intervals.

before: Absolute parameter accuracy would require a geometrically faithful reference or measured dataset with known modifications, compatible boundary conditions, calibrated measurement scale and resolved angular waveforms. A physically modified FE contour must also update elastic stiffness and contact geometry. The modified-contour control tests the elastic consequence of removal while keeping the candidate contact geometry unchanged by construction. It is a controlled test of a theorem hypothesis, not a validation of a complete manufactured profile, contact transitions or inverse reconstruction. The results define what follows from the declared operator and identify which additional information physical reconstruction requires.
after: Absolute parameter accuracy requires a geometrically faithful reference or measured data with known modifications, compatible boundary conditions, calibrated scale and resolved angular waveforms. The material-removal control in Section 4.5 reassembles elasticity while keeping candidate contact geometry fixed, isolating a theorem hypothesis. The full-cycle generator in Section 4.9 updates both the modified geometry and its FE stiffness, whereas its inverse retains nominal elasticity. Neither uses a certified manufactured root fillet. These experiments delimit the consequences of declared assumptions and identify what physical reconstruction still requires.

before: Limitations and outlook. All inversions use synthetic data, and the external reference is a published set of finite-element amplitudes rather than measured waveforms from gears with known modifications. The analytical operator reduces each candidate pair to one effective normal contact, and the finite-element generator is two-dimensional plane-strain; both are frictionless and quasistatic. The gap-only inverse operators retain fixed sections, normals and contact coordinates; the separate material-removal control relaxes the fixed-section assumption by reassembling elasticity. Dynamic effects, mounting deviations [17], wide-face effects [16] and the manufactured root fillet are outside this reduction. The finite-element gap tests share the nominal sections with the analytical model, and the omitted engagement-transition phases may carry information that cannot be counted until their contact is resolved. Profile-likelihood thresholds are nominal diagnostics because discrepancy is deterministic. Future work should (i) apply the support diagnostic to measured transmission error from gears with certified relief, (ii) resolve engagement transitions and fillet contact in the forward model, and (iii) replace the assumed noise scale and nominal likelihood thresholds by a calibrated discrepancy model within a Bayesian framework [40,41]. The stress controls in Section 4.8 relax the independent-noise and same-compliance assumptions and add periodic errors and estimated covariance under specified synthetic alternatives. They do not resolve the omitted FE transition stations or provide measured waveform calibration. Supplementary Table S27 maps each remaining evidence gap to a concrete follow-up experiment; the new periodic-error and covariance controls address part of the final row, while the physical follow-ups remain unperformed. A single deterministic FE waveform difference would characterize phase-dependent discrepancy, but would not by itself estimate a stochastic discrepancy covariance without replication or additional modelling assumptions.
after: Limitations and outlook. All inversions use synthetic data; the external amplitude reference is a published FE benchmark, not measured TE from gears with certified modifications. The analytical operator reduces each pair to one effective normal contact. All FE experiments are frictionless, quasistatic and plane-strain; dynamic effects, mounting deviations [17], wide-face effects [16] and the manufactured root fillet remain outside this reduction. Historical gap-only inverses retain fixed sections, normals and coordinates. Section 4.9 resolves the complete discrete cycle for the assumed contour with a separate full-geometry generator, but its moving-contact inverse retains nominal elasticity. Closure errors, two-grid changes and unsuccessful optimization attempts are reported; continuum-converged inversion is not established. Selected independent-solver checks validate neither the complete cycle nor physical relief recovery. The stress controls add periodic errors and known/estimated covariance under prescribed synthetic alternatives, without measured calibration. Future work should apply the support diagnostic to measured TE with certified relief, characterize fillet and face-width effects, and calibrate discrepancy before assigning physical uncertainty through a Bayesian framework [40,41]. Table S27 maps the original follow-ups; the discrete-cycle and periodic-error parts are now addressed conditionally, while physical validation remains open. A single deterministic FE difference does not identify a stochastic discrepancy covariance without replication or additional assumptions. The current archive also remains without a repository DOI.

before: The stress controls extend the numerical evidence to correlated noise, known and estimated covariance, periodic measurement errors, gain and a change of compliance formulation. With 200 paired deeper-case realizations, a 5% gain raises median scaled dedendum error from 0.0916 to 1.86; the 95% paired-bootstrap interval for the difference of medians is [1.44, 3.32]. Residual screening and noise-free transfer quantify consequences within the assumed operators, without establishing physical profile recovery. The defensible outcome remains an operator-conditioned account of observability and uncertainty, together with a pre-inversion support check. Independent mechanical and experimental validation remains necessary for physical reconstruction.

before: Data availability. Current code, raw observations, all 1100 selected stress cases, 3300 final fitting attempts and 300 covariance-pilot attempts, bootstrap replicates, transfer diagnostics, source hashes and construction files are supplied in MMT_reproducibility_v18.zip. Earlier numerical campaigns are preserved unchanged. The preceding version-13 baseline is public at https://github.com/romusan/gears-inversion-reproducibility/tree/manuscript-v13; it does not include subsequent controls or this revision. No repository DOI is currently assigned.
after: Data availability. MMT_reproducibility_v19.zip supplies the current construction and analysis code, full-cycle observations, saved contact states, all inverse attempts, numerical audits, software/source provenance and a SHA-256 manifest. The preceding v18 archive preserves 1100 selected stress cases, 3300 final fitting attempts and 300 covariance-pilot attempts; it and the selected-phase mechanical evidence are included as unchanged companion archives.
